newsitem.title: USA: LDC debt up with Treasuries, Bulgaria outperforms.
newsitem.headline: LDC debt up with Treasuries, Bulgaria outperforms.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices wound down the New York trading session on a higher note with Bulgaria debt seen as the outperformer, traders said.

"Bulgaria certainly outperformed others today," said Richard Segal, head of fixed income research at Santander Investments. "There's increasing excitement over the possibility of a currency board coming on line early next month."
Bulgaria FLRB, hard hit on Friday, rebounded in Monday's trading session gaining 1-3/8 points to trade at a 40-3/4 bid.

On Monday, Bulgarian Prime Minister Zhan Videnov said the government planned a package of measures to stabilze the economy and hoped parliament could vote on the introduction of a currency board regime on January 2nd.
"The reason the market is optimistic is essentially because if they vote against it (currency board) it's essentially a vote to call an early election," Segal said.
"Parliament will not likely let it self out of office... because the socialist majority would be highly likely to lose that election given the poor state of the economy there," Segal added.
In general, traders said Brady bonds rebounded on Monday following Friday's volatile trading session, when U.S. Treasuries slid heavily dragging bradies down with them.
Argentina FRBs traded up 3/8 to 86-1/8 bid and Brazil C gained 1/4 to a 73 bid, traders said.
During Friday's stormy session, Brazil and Mexico brady bonds widened 10 to 20 basis points while Argentina and Venezuela bradies widened by 30 to 40 basis points, traders added.
"It's been impressive...all markets have rebounded from Greenspan's comments last week," said Brian Barish head of emerging market research at Lazard Freres & Co.

Comments late Thursday, by Fed chairman Alan Greenspan warning against "irrational" market exuberance, sent U.S. Treasuries tumbling. Later, Treasuries were able to regain some ground following the U.S. Labor Department's release of a weaker-than-expected payrolls report.
"There's so much high-powered liquitidy in the U.S. capital markets and the U.S. bond market right now from domestic as well as foreign sources," Barish said.
"It seems to me that it may take more than a stern verbal warning if you really wanted to engineer a correction...for that to actually happen," Barish added.
Among other issues, Mexico Pars were up 1/8 to 73-1/8 while Venezuela Pars gained 3/8 to trade at 75-3/8 bid, traders said.
Russia Min Fin 3 also made up some lost ground trading up 3/8 to 83-1/2 bid.
